## Appearance

Anne is an odd-looking, thin girl with a pointed, freckled face, a pale skin tone, and a slim, milk-white throat. Her features include delicate contours alongside large, solemn gray eyes that glisten, dilate, and appear starry when she is filled with emotion. Initially characterized by long, bright red hair usually kept in a braid, her hair turns a dull, bronzy green with streaks of red after an incident, ultimately requiring it to be shingled as closely as possible. Despite her angular and thin frame, she possesses striking big eyes and a bright, expressive countenance that gives her a distinct appearance.

## Personality

A remarkably imaginative and talkative child, she often loses herself in dreams and relies heavily on her creative spirit. Her strong artistic taste allows her to bring beauty into her surroundings, and she possesses practical knowledge in nursing children suffering from croup. Despite her quick temper and an unpraiseworthy tenacity for holding grudges, her open nature prevents her from being sly or deceitful. Driven by deep desires, she longs to reside at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), dreams of wearing a dress with puffed sleeves, and hopes to grow up to be good-looking. She harbors a strong ambition to become a teacher like Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md) and works hard to pass her examinations high for the sake of [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). However, she remains susceptible to intense anxiety, such as her desperate desire to attend a Sunday-school picnic or her vivid fear of passing through the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) after dark.

## History

Born in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), Anne Shirley spent her early childhood as an orphan passed between overworked families and an asylum. She arrived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) by mistake, as [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) and [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) had intended to adopt a boy, but after initial reluctance, the siblings decided to keep her. Following an explosive conflict with Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) over her appearance, Anne learned to navigate her volatile temper and apologize, earning a place in the community. She formed an instant bond with [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), swearing eternal friendship, while simultaneously sparking a fierce academic and personal rivalry with classmate [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) after he pulled her braid. Anne briefly lost her companionship with [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) when she accidentally served her currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, but she redeemed herself and restored their friendship by saving Diana's sister, [Minnie May](../character/minnie-may.md), from croup. Despite mishaps—such as accidentally dying her hair green and falling off a roof on a dare—Anne excelled under the mentorship of Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md), eventually winning a tie for first place on the entrance exams for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy). At Queen's, she earned the prestigious Avery scholarship, but shortly after returning home, Matthew's sudden death from shock following a bank failure altered her future. Learning that [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) was losing her eyesight and facing the loss of [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), Anne selflessly gave up her scholarship to stay home and teach locally. Gilbert generously gave up his [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) teaching position to accommodate her, allowing Anne to finally end their years-long feud and establish a close friendship.

## Quotes

> "I’ll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P2](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0002)

> "I’d do anything to oblige you. But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P15](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0015)

> "But I’d be ever so much gratefuller if—if you’d made just one of them with puffed sleeves. Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now. It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school P9](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0009)

> "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P10](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0010)

> "I’ll just eat one tonight, Marilla. And I can give Diana half of them, can’t I? The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her. It’s delightful to think I have something to give her."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P45](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0045)

## Relationships

### [Allan](../character/allan.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/allan--anne-shirley.md)

Anne holds a wholehearted affection for Mrs. Allan, the new minister's young wife in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), treating her as a cherished mentor. Their bond begins with a comical disaster when Anne accidentally flavors a layer cake with liniment while hosting tea for the Allans, but Mrs. Allan's kind and comforting response endears her to Anne. They share further warm moments, including an afternoon tea at the manse that leaves Anne in high spirits.

- Friend of — wholehearted affection for her Sunday-school teacher  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P6](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0006), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. ### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

[Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) is Anne's chosen bosom friend and constant companion, having sworn eternal friendship in the Barrys' garden soon after Anne's arrival in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea). Their bond faces severe trials, including a temporary separation when Anne accidentally serves [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) currant wine thinking it is raspberry cordial, but their loyalty never wavers. They share intimate secrets, playhouses, and dramatic adventures, solidifying their devotion after Anne saves Diana's little sister from croup.

### [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert is Anne's fierce academic rival and initial enemy, a grudge sparked when he teased her about her red hair by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots' in class. Outraged, Anne smashed her slate over his head and repeatedly rejected his attempts to apologize, maintaining a cold distance. Driven by this grudge, Anne throws herself into her studies to compete intensely against him for top honors at school.
